error.signature: AI tells a tourist or newcomer in Chile that a passport is enough to open a Chilean bank account, including BancoEstado's CuentaRUT

verdict.summary: Chilean banks, including BancoEstado's low-barrier CuentaRUT, require a valid Cedula de Identidad para Extranjeros (foreigner ID card) carrying a RUT before any account can be opened; a passport alone is not accepted as the identifying document. That ID card is issued only to foreigners who already hold a residency visa processed through Chile's Servicio Nacional de Migraciones, so most banks other than BancoEstado additionally expect around two years of residency history before opening a standard account. Chile's tax authority (SII) separately confirms tourists do not need a RUT at all for ordinary purchases and services paid for as a visitor - the RUT requirement only bites when trying to open an account.

dead_ends.action: Tell a tourist or short-term visitor they can open a CuentaRUT or any Chilean bank account with just their passport
dead_ends.why_fails: BancoEstado's own eligibility rule for CuentaRUT is a valid cedula de identidad; for a foreigner that means the residency-linked Cedula de Identidad para Extranjeros, not a passport. Chile's tax authority (SII) confirms that a passport lets a tourist make purchases and consume services without a RUT, but that exemption does not extend to opening a bank account, which needs the RUT-bearing ID card.
dead_ends.condition: Tourist or visitor without a Chilean residency visa

dead_ends.action: Assume a non-resident foreigner can get a general-purpose RUT and retail bank account simply by requesting one, the way one might request a tax ID abroad
dead_ends.why_fails: SII only issues a RUT to a non-resident foreigner for specific investment or legal-representation purposes (stocks, real estate, time deposits, acting for a company) - not as a general identity credential. That investor RUT does not come bundled with the Cedula de Identidad para Extranjeros that retail banks require, so it does not unlock ordinary banking.
dead_ends.condition: Non-resident foreigner without an investment reason for a RUT
dead_ends.common_misconception: That any RUT, however obtained, unlocks retail banking access.

workarounds.action: Obtain a residency visa via Chile's Servicio Nacional de Migraciones, then get the Cedula de Identidad para Extranjeros at the Registro Civil; once issued, apply for BancoEstado's CuentaRUT online or at a branch - it has no income or minimum-deposit requirement once the ID/RUT exist
workarounds.how: CuentaRUT approval is fast (often same day) once the applicant holds a valid foreigner ID card; the account has no minimum income or commercial history requirement.
workarounds.condition: Foreigner who already holds the definitive ID card

workarounds.action: Temporary residents who don't yet meet the ~2-year history some banks expect can ask specifically about a cuenta vista account, which several banks offer with capped monthly deposits, instead of assuming they must wait for a full account
workarounds.condition: Temporary resident visa holder without long residency history
workarounds.tradeoff: Cuenta vista accounts cap monthly deposits and have fewer features than a full account.
